title: [main][Performance][KV Pool] Cache layer-invariant masked_block_runs across layers
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`masked_block_runs` is a pure-Python O(block-count) scan called from `_process_save_for_layer_batch` / `_process_load_for_layer_batch`. Within one scheduling step its inputs — the per-group reachability mask and the save/load block range — are **layer-invariant**, but the layer loop in `process_layer_data` recomputes it for every local layer (e.g. 61x on a 61-layer model).

Profiling the layerwise path shows the calls are bimodal: ~8.8us for decode-step ranges vs up to ~13.2ms for long-prompt prefills (thousands of blocks scanned one by one). Multiplied by the layer count, the redundant rescans cost hundreds of milliseconds of pure Python on the forward critical path.

This PR memoizes the runs per step, keyed by `(path, req_id, group_id, start_block, end_block)`:

- save path: fully layer-invariant → scanned once, reused by all layers
- load path: `load_start_block` varies for independent layers (MTP/draft) → they keep distinct cache entries
- the cache is cleared at the top of `process_layer_data`, before the layer loop

No behavior change; the per-layer `LayerTransferTask` construction is untouched.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit test added: `test_masked_block_runs_cached_across_layers` in `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py` — asserts identical runs across two layers with a holey mask, a single cache entry, and per-step cache clearing.
- `pytest tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py` (mocked CPU UTs): all `TestKVPoolWorkerProcessLayerData` cases pass; `test_mooncake_layerwise.py` / `test_kv_transfer.py` / `test_pool_scheduler.py` suites pass unchanged.
- NPU verification and CI runs still to be done (draft).

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607
